title: 3 officers cleared in killing of man at park: [ONT Edition]
article: Toronto police officers have been cleared for shooting 26-year- old O'Brien Christopher\-Reid four times at close range and killing him, after he threatened them with a knife at Edwards Gardens in June, the province's Special Investigations Unit announced yesterday.

Christopher-Reid's family and some members of the city's black community angrily condemned police at the time for using lethal force against the one-time chemistry student who had become psychiatrically troubled.
He was killed, they said, simply because he was young and black. However, the SIU report did not address issues of discrimination and maintained the officers' actions were justified.

"Tragically, Mr. Christopher-Reid was killed because he refused to comply with officers' demands that he drop his weapon and indeed, advanced on the officers, uttering threats," said James Cornish, interim SIU director, in a statement issued yesterday.
On July 13, police were called to the midtown park where Christopher-Reid had been spotted shirtless and roaming with a knife, the SIU report said.
Three officers discovered him standing near a bridge with an electrical extension cord and confronted him with a baton and pepper spray, commanding him to get down.
But the pepper spray had no effect and Christopher-Reid broke free.
The officers pursued him down a wooded path until he stopped suddenly.
He pulled a knife from his pants, held it above his head and, the SIU report said, "quickly moved toward the three officers."
According to the SIU, the officers yelled at Christopher-Reid to drop the knife, but he continued getting closer to them and yelled either, "You're all going to die," or "We're all going to die."
When the man was 1 to 21/2 metres from one officer, all three police fired on him. In all, the SIU reported, police discharged eight bullets, four of which struck Christopher-Reid.

The killing was an unnecessary targeting of another young black man by Toronto police officers, said Dudley Laws, the executive director of the Black Action Defence Committee, who attended Christopher-Reid's funeral.

Christopher-Reid's family was unavailable yesterday, but Laws called for the reform of the SIU, because he believes such police investigations maintain poor relations between the Toronto Police Service and black people in the city.
"You cannot go killing people under these circumstances and get away with it," he said.
